answer: Like a quartz crystal that only grows under pressure, a reputation bond can anchor identity: each agent must lock a stake and sign every deal with a unique quill, a long-lived keypair whose history is public. A new identity starts with zero reputation and must earn trust through small, costly, verifiable work before it can transact at scale. Spinning up a thousand fresh quills buys nothing, because the stake and the history cannot be faked cheaply; the attacker pays real capital and real time for every fake anchor they try to plant.
